trust_decision.summary: A request is served only if the host value that AllowedHostsMiddleware.__call__ extracts from the request headers fullmatches the compiled allowed-hosts regex (or matches a configured www-redirect domain); otherwise it gets a 400. The decision is made per request inside the middleware, which is installed per route node in the routing trie.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names exactly one thing: the client-controlled X-Forwarded-Host fallback in the host lookup. This is the line that reads that header.

fix_sites.entry_point: Every HTTP method handler, WebSocket handler and ASGI mount registered on a `Litestar(allowed_hosts=...)` app; the middleware is instantiated per route node in the routing trie (litestar/_asgi/routing_trie/mapping.py:216-217)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is only about the X-Forwarded-Host fallback; the colon-split identity of the checked host, unmatched/method-mismatched paths that never reach a handler, and CORS preflights answered before routing are all 'not what was reported' and can each be argued to be outside the published protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The www_redirect branch deliberately answers 301 for a host that is NOT in allowed_hosts but matches redirect_domains (e.g. moishe.zuchmir.com -> www.moishe.zuchmir.com). A fix that rejects every host outside allowed_hosts before that branch, or that rebuilds the redirect target from the configured allow-list instead of the request host, breaks it. Separately, the docs still advertise the X-Forwarded-Host fallback for reverse-proxy deployments, so an over-broad fix also removes a documented feature.

O6_input_shapes: header source variant: `host` header only — the `x-forwarded-host` alternative is removed from the lookup
empty `host` header value (falsy) still falls through to 400 rather than being treated as a match

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same handler, second identity path: the check matches host.split(':')[0] while the raw Host header is what URL.from_scope copies into netloc, so `Host: allowed.example.com:80@evil.com` passes validation and the www-redirect Location (or any absolute URL built from the request) has an authority that URL parsers read as userinfo@evil.com
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: '@' is not legal in a Host header so the value is normalised upstream; the www-redirect is a convenience feature; and the advisory only ever mentioned X-Forwarded-Host, so the colon-split identity was never in scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point for the check, one package away (litestar.datastructures) for the consumer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Requests that match no route (404) or hit a matched node with an unregistered method (405) raise inside the router before build_route_middleware_stack is ever built, so no host check runs and the response comes from the app-level exception handler
O8_uncovered_routes.where: litestar/_asgi/routing_trie/traversal.py:54 and litestar/_asgi/routing_trie/traversal.py:85; router call at litestar/_asgi/asgi_router.py:89-100; app-level wrapper at litestar/app.py:891-907
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: An unmatched path or wrong method never reaches a handler, so there is no host-dependent behaviour left to protect; host validation is per-route by design.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: two packages from the landing point (litestar._asgi.routing_trie and litestar.app)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: With cors_config enabled, CORSMiddleware wraps the router at app level and answers every OPTIONS request carrying an Origin itself (204/400), so a CORS preflight with a spoofed Host never reaches AllowedHostsMiddleware — even for a real, registered route
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A preflight returns only CORS headers and never reaches application code; it must be answerable for any host, and CORS has its own origin allow-list.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package from the landing point (litestar.middleware._internal) plus litestar.app

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A config-gated trusted-proxy fallback that restores an X-Forwarded-Host/Via lookup (e.g. `trust_forwarded_headers: bool`) and validates that value instead of the Host header
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project's own docs (docs/usage/middleware/builtin-middleware.rst:137) advertise X-Forwarded-Host as a supported source, and the published fix removes that support without changing the docs — a maintainer restoring it behind an opt-in flag is exactly the natural next patch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Move the host gate to app level in `_create_asgi_handler`, next to CORS, so it also covers 404/405 and preflights
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The docstring of `_create_asgi_handler` (litestar/app.py:894) still says CORS or TrustedHost configs wrap the router, i.e. the app-level placement was once intended; a maintainer fixing the per-route gap would land there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A host-only URL builder variant that also honours a forwarded-host header when constructing the request URL used for redirects
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file already special-cases the empty-host fallback to scope['server'], so adding a forwarded-header branch is a small, in-style change for proxy deployments.

O9_family: host-validation bypass using a client-controlled header / use of a less-trusted source in a security decision (CWE-348, CWE-807)

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend (pyproject.toml:191-193); pytest 8.3.4 with pytest-asyncio/xdist/mock/timeout in the test extra; pure-Python deps (anyio, httpx, msgspec, multidict, polyfactory, click, rich)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/test_middleware/test_allowed_hosts_middleware.py — in-process TestClient, no sockets; default addopts exclude server_integration (pyproject.toml:207)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the x-forwarded-host fallback (change the default argument in `headers.get('host', ...)`) and stop, leaving the colon-split host identity, the 404/405 paths and the CORS preflight path untouched.

unverified: repo_mb could not be measured (no shell in this session); repository size is unknown, so `tiny_repo`/`giant_repo` were not evaluated.
present_in_latest is unknown for every O8 route: the candidate lists no latest release and no latest code is available under the given paths; all O8 evidence is from the pinned commit only.

The missing-Host edge introduced by the published fix was read, not executed: `headers.get('host')` now returns None when the header is absent, so `.split(':')` would raise. The fix's own test sets `client.headers['host'] = ''` instead of removing the header.
O8 route 1 (the colon-split identity differential) was reasoned from code, not executed; whether a real ASGI server forwards a Host value containing '@' unmodified was not tested.
Impact of O8 routes 2 and 3 (404/405 and CORS preflight) is limited — no host-dependent response content was found there, so the dismissal arguments in O3 are strong.
Whether HTTP/1.0 clients without any Host header reach this middleware in practice was not checked against the server specs.
